steps.audit_note: The swing did not drive the nail. The hammer is a substitute (64 g). It came down five times, touched the nail head on the first two strokes and otherwise pressed on the block, which stayed on the table instead of being held by the left hand. The nail reading was back at 0.0 mm once the hammer withdrew. The motion was not a face-down blow: at the strokes the hammer's long axis was 54–65° below horizontal, a push along the handle with the top of the head.

audit_note: Audited 2026-11-23: FAIL. This run was reported as a pass of the official t08 check. The audit found that the hammer strike did not drive the nail. With a substitute hammer (64 g), the right hand brought the hammer down five times; it grazed the nail twice and otherwise pressed on the block, and when it withdrew the nail was no deeper than at the start. The nail had already slid down until its tip rested on the table before the robot moved, so the depth reading could only grow if the tip sank into the table contact or the block was lifted off the nail. The reported 11.8 mm was read at tick 1179, while the left hand was raising the block and the hammer was about 0.56 m away. The left hand held the block at least 30 mm up for about 2.6 s and then dropped it; at the end of the episode the reading is 0.0 mm. The 'official' check never measured a valid hit: it marked the hit valid because the depth number was at least 0.25 mm. What stands: nothing in this run counts as a pass or a demo.

audit.finding: Fail: with a substitute 64 g hammer the right hand swung at the nail five times, grazing it twice and otherwise pressing on the block, and left the nail no deeper; the reported 11.8 mm depth came later from the left hand lifting the block off a nail that had already slid down to the table before the episode began (hammer 0.56 m away), the block was then dropped, and the official valid-hit term was never measured.
